old: - `ssdl-systems-thinking-foundations-decision-making.md`, Social System Design Lab / Brown School at Washington University in St. Louis (*Methods Briefs Series 1: Systems Thinking Foundations*, 2021; five briefs — 1.02 Complex Problems / 1.03 Mental Models / 1.05 Feedback Perspective / 1.06 Accumulations / 1.07 System Archetypes). Five characteristics of complex problems as triage diagnostic (dynamic / multi-stakeholder / time delays / unintended consequences / accumulations); broken-ankle test ("you don't need to make a system dynamics model about it") for when systems-thinking is overkill; mental-model surfacing as decision-quality precondition with sticky-models-among-the-unaffected warning; CLDs as decision-hypotheses (not answers) and intervention design as loop-structure change; stock-and-flow as the structural form of history-dependence with the blank-slate failure mode; five Kim (1993) archetypes — Fixes that Fail, Success to the Successful, Shifting the Burden, Drifting Goals, Limits to Growth — as recurring decision-trap patterns.
